source_method: Pinned M03 full FFN; only ingress/assembly changed
scope: One local transfer-dataflow combination; three implementation variants, not three architectures

builds.v1: Compile/host PASS; emitted full30-row up/gate transfer per6-row tile, static cost closure; no NPU
builds.v2: Compact source created, but assembly DMA reads beyond source range; compiler rejects; no executable
builds.v3: Replace assembly DMA with raw FP4 Sub copy; full compile/host and basic NPU PASS

interpretation: Smaller emitted ingress tasks are achieved in v3, while full decode and dot remain three streams each.
Source coverage alone did not constrain v1 emitted transfer volume; v3 graph confirms intended payload after the raw Sub repair.
Static pre-RMS-to-amax gap shrinks, but pre-RMS starts later; amax and final input broadcast are not earlier.
Whole-kernel NPU result has no qualifying gain. The actual internal contribution of copies/arbitration is not measured or inferred from the static schedule.
No new top10-capable submission established; E104 remains adopted.
closure: Close this prototype after the basic screen under the5% experiment-budget rule; no tile sweep, repeated screening or official submission. A small one-job difference is not a statistical significance claim.
retry_condition: A concrete change to transfer arbitration or full-buffer assembly/materialization cost. Merely changing the number of chunks is not a new mechanism.
